snippets.text: SemiAnalysis says Inferact, the makers of vLLM, and Google made a first preliminary TPUv7 submission for the 2.8-trillion-parameter Kimi K3, claiming strong performance per total cost against Nvidia GB200 NVL72, B300 and AMD MI355.
snippets.why: If it holds up, Google's TPUs become a credible rival to Nvidia for serving the largest open models, and vLLM's makers are driving it.

snippets.text: TestingCatalog says Anthropic's Claude personal-finance feature, which reads bank data through Plaid and builds dashboards, has been renamed from 'Claude Money' in the latest app update, and may launch soon. Unconfirmed.
snippets.why: Andrew Curran separately called the product 'Claude Monet'; Anthropic has announced nothing, so the name and the timing both rest on app strings.

snippets.text: Hugging Face's Thomas Wolf says the most built-upon model on the Hub is Black Forest Labs' FLUX.1-dev, with 43,000 derivative models, ahead of Llama and Qwen.
snippets.why: He also says Europe trained about 8% of the Hub's open-model compute but accounts for about 18% of what is built on top of it, his own estimate.

snippets.text: International Cyber Digest says a draft Chinese export-control list would require licences to export AI that finds five or more unknown severe flaws in a major OS, or models above 2 trillion parameters.
snippets.why: Chinese ministries published the draft on October 16 for comment until November 15; it reads as restrictions and registration rather than a blanket ban.

snippets.text: Developer finereli released whatsapp-mcp, an MIT-licensed read-only server that lets an AI agent search your WhatsApp messages, running on Cloudflare Workers. It had 14 GitHub stars and 25 Show HN points.
snippets.why: The README says it breaks WhatsApp's terms, stores messages in plaintext in your own Cloudflare account, and has been tested on only one account.

snippets.text: Researcher Elvis Saravia summarises a paper in which an engine generates data-analysis training environments from scratch; reinforcement learning on 2,135 tasks lifts Qwen3.6-35B-A3B by 20.9 points on DABstep-Hard.
snippets.why: Because the generating process is known, answers can be checked, which the authors use to train without distilled trajectories; the results are the paper's own.

snippets.text: Fal says Kotoba's speech APIs are now live on its platform, covering real-time speech translation with text and audio output, live transcription, preset-voice speech generation and timestamped transcripts.
snippets.why: It puts a Japanese-built speech stack behind the same hosted API developers already use for image and video models.

snippets.text: Tibo Sottiaux says the Codex desktop app now lets you edit previous messages within a thread, a long-requested feature that he admits took too long to ship.
snippets.why: Editing an earlier prompt in place, rather than starting over, is a basic chat feature the coding app had been missing.

snippets.text: Developer Theo posted a demo of T3 Code, his coding-agent app, running threads on remote VPSs and Linux boxes, and compared it with OpenAI's Codex app, mostly on local threads.
snippets.why: Running agent sessions across several machines from one window is the pitch of the new wave of third-party coding front ends.

snippets.text: International Cyber Digest says Nvidia denies it has killed the RTX 5090, with senior vice president Jeff Fisher saying the flagship keeps shipping though supply is constrained; European prices run near €7,000.
snippets.why: The denial answers leakers who said the chips were being redirected to professional and AI cards; supply, not a cancellation, is Nvidia's stated problem.

snippets.text: Researchers from McAuley Lab introduced CarryOn, a context runtime for long-running agents that they say gains 5.8% on OSWorld 2.0 and 7.0% on BrowseComp-Plus while cutting token use by 51.9% and 22.9%.
snippets.why: Instead of replaying an agent's whole history, it carries forward reusable task objects, which is why the token bill falls; results are the authors' own.

snippets.text: The vLLM project says all six D3 decision models, from 0.6B to 27B parameters, now have merged vLLM recipes, and that D3 ranked first on both Jev Decision Index 0.3.2 boards.
snippets.why: The recipes let teams self-host D3 on vLLM, though the 66.3 text and 71.3 vision scores come from the project's citation of the index.

snippets.text: World launched a World ID suite for banks that includes World ID for Agents, which lets a person delegate their proof of humanity to an AI agent, The Block reports.
snippets.why: It is World's first industry-specific product, and it names no bank customer yet, only design partners including OpenExchange, Bain Capital and VanEck.

snippets.text: Peking University and Ant International researchers say Claude Opus 5 scored highest on BizBench, their 50-task business-agent test, with 64.0% strict success, ahead of GPT-6 Sol at 61.3%.
snippets.why: Only 40.0% of tasks were completed in all three of GPT-6 Sol's runs, which suggests consistency, not peak score, is the hard part for business agents.

snippets.text: Tencent Hunyuan researchers say TreeOPSD, a critic-free training method for long-horizon agents, lifted a Qwen3-30B-A3B model to 21.20 average Deep Research accuracy from 17.59 for TreePO.
snippets.why: The authors also report it beats GRPO by 4.97 points on that average, though the results are the paper's own and no code link is given.

snippets.text: Developer Jared Siegel argues in a blog post, now on the Hacker News front page with 75 points, that engineers should run their own LLM proxy to see keys, models, clients and cache misses.
snippets.why: Provider dashboards show little about agent traffic, he says, so a self-hosted proxy with virtual keys is his answer; he names no specific product.

snippets.text: SemiconductorsX relays that Intel's CEO told Nikkei that Moonshot's Kimi, Zhipu's GLM and DeepSeek are not technically behind Anthropic or OpenAI, and are much cheaper to use.
snippets.why: The claim comes from a chipmaker chief with a stake in the China debate, and it is relayed secondhand, so the Nikkei interview itself was not checked.

snippets.text: OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux says the company worked with OpenCode to restore service for users who are also OpenAI API customers and refund credits drawn in an attack, and offers defenders 'Daybreak Blue' access.
snippets.why: The post is OpenAI's own account of the fix; the attack's scope and cause are not described in it, and OpenCode has not been checked here.

snippets.text: Stripe says agentic transactions on its Link checkout rose 38x in September, with payment volume up 20x and retail leading, according to data it gave Upstarts Media exclusively.
snippets.why: Link's head of consumer product, Dan Hill, told Upstarts about 200 agents now use Link, up from about 70 in September.

snippets.text: Artificial Analysis lists DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 at 45 on its Intelligence Index, second among 121 models in its class, at $0.30 input and $1.20 output per million tokens, with a 1M-token context.
snippets.why: The firm says the model is open-weight under an MIT licence; the score is Artificial Analysis's own measurement, and DeepSeek has not been checked on the 1017 changes.

snippets.text: Show HN: Project STROT, an MIT-licensed Python library that uses an LLM once to compile a decision pipeline, then runs a 144M-parameter model locally on CPU, about 60 ms per record.
snippets.why: Its author reports 92.5% on a 398-record routing test against 74.8% for a naive baseline; the benchmarks are self-reported and the repo has 22 stars.

snippets.text: Theo, who makes the T3 Code app, says that over the last two weeks more than 60% of its users who used OpenAI's Codex also used Claude Code.
snippets.why: It is one developer's usage figure from his own app, not an industry survey, but it suggests coding-agent users are not picking a single tool.

snippets.text: Commentator Kimmonismus shared a screenshot of Claude flagging that a user's Mac was running a cryptominer they had not installed, while the user was building a temperature app with it.
snippets.why: The post has about 470 likes, but it rests on a single screenshot and nobody has independently confirmed what the malware was or how it got there.

snippets.text: SemiAnalysis says 60GW of datacenter capacity is under construction, 50GW could be added in 2027 alone, and $1.3 trillion of leases have been signed this year, with the shortage possibly shifting to chips.
snippets.why: If the firm's leading indicators hold, power and buildings are no longer the main constraint on AI capacity, and chip supply becomes the next bottleneck.

snippets.text: OpenCode confirmed a security breach that may have exposed users' OpenAI, Anthropic and Google API keys, affecting 1.4% of Console users, The Hacker News reports, and urged affected users to revoke their keys.
snippets.why: Some users report unauthorised AI usage charges, so anyone who stored provider keys in OpenCode's Console should rotate them now rather than wait for a fuller account.

snippets.text: AI-news account MaxForAI says it has been told a high-profile model launches today with better agentic ability than DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017 and a lower price, citing leaked tests; no lab has confirmed it.
snippets.why: It is an unconfirmed tip, but it would put pressure on DeepSeek's cheap-agent pitch within days of its own quiet release.

snippets.text: Nvidia's Vera team told Wccftech the Vera CPU is 1.5 times faster than Grace and up to 2 times faster than x86 on sequential agentic tasks, and is now sold standalone.
snippets.why: Nvidia argues agentic workloads are pushing CPU design back toward single-thread speed over core counts, and that its monolithic die avoids chiplet latency.

snippets.text: Elon Musk posted that next year he will give one of his SpaceX shares to every kid in America, calling it the first of many; the post had over 123,000 likes.
snippets.why: Bloomberg reports the pledge came hours after Anthropic said it would put 5% of its shares in a public benefit fund, and the post gives no mechanism or date.

snippets.text: A Disney court filing says it will offer jobs to at least 60 Character.AI employees, with an estimated annual pay of $60 million, TechCrunch reports, and most offers were accepted.
snippets.why: Disney agreed to buy some Character.AI assets for $20 million in a stalking-horse bid, so a higher offer from another buyer is still possible.

snippets.text: Brian Roemmele says he built a free Grok Bot whose only job is to phone a restaurant and book a table, and says it called an Italian restaurant in Temecula for four people.
snippets.why: The claim is Roemmele's own, shown in a photo post, and it has not been independently tested.

snippets.text: A creator says he hacked his TV and PS5 with Claude Code in one night, blocking 37 tracking domains on the TV and cutting the PS5's boot time from 41 seconds to 9.
snippets.why: The results are the poster's own claims, shown in a video, and the post does not say which TV model he used.

snippets.text: Developer sorenxet says he built a cozy fishing game with Claude Opus 5.5, Blender and Unity 6 by connecting them through blender-mcp and unity-mcp and writing a one-page game doc first.
snippets.why: His advice is to avoid asking for 'a fishing game' in one prompt; the post includes a video walkthrough, and the result has not been independently tested.

snippets.text: The Decoder reports the share of junior roles among Anthropic's new technical hires fell from 27% to 9% since early 2025, and that its AI agents logged six times as many hours as humans by August.
snippets.why: The figures come from researchers' work cited by The Decoder, which warns of a 'tragedy of the cognitive commons' if junior roles vanish.

snippets.text: Bloomberg reports Meta said an automated security system mistakenly suspended the Instagram account of the No Kings Coalition during nationwide demonstrations, and its headline names a Claude AI tool as the trigger.
snippets.why: The full article was not accessible, so details of how Claude was involved, and any response from Anthropic, are unconfirmed.

snippets.text: The Verge reports a Philadelphia woman, Carolyn Marvin, was arrested for disorderly conduct after blocking an Uber delivery robot, saying she protests the robots for taking human delivery jobs.
snippets.why: The account comes from The Verge, citing her interview with ABC13; the robot's maker and the charge outcome were not stated in the excerpt reviewed.
